Timeline::host¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::HostAny Timeline::host() const

What It Does¶

host() materializes the timeline as owning host-side epoch nanoseconds and packages the result according to its cardinality and rank. It is intended for C++ integration points that need ordinary values rather than temporal methods: serializers, database bindings, custom kernels, and foreign-function bridges.

The returned HostAny has three possible payloads:

Source

Predicate

Accessor

Payload

any one-position timeline

is_scalar()

scalar()

one std::int64_t

rank 1 with zero or multiple positions

is_vector()

vector()

std::vector<std::int64_t>

rank 2 or 3 with zero or multiple positions

is_array()

array()

data, shape, timezone, contiguity

The first row is intentionally based on cardinality, not rank. Consequently a shape [1] timeline produces a scalar host payload even though Timeline::is_scalar() is false. Check the HostAny predicate before opening its payload rather than predicting the variant from the source rank.

Epoch Representation¶

Every exported integer is nanoseconds since the Unix epoch in UTC. Timezone metadata accompanies the payload, but it does not alter those integers. NaT is represented by Timeline::kNaT, the minimum signed 64-bit value.

Returns¶

An owning Timeline::HostAny. Its data remains valid independently of the source timeline.

Examples¶

Example 1. Open scalar and vector payloads after checking their kinds.

auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto vector = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-02-29T12:30:00Z", "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"
});
auto scalar_host = scalar.host();
auto vector_host = vector.host();

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar host: scalar=" << scalar_host.is_scalar()
          << ", value=" << scalar_host.scalar()
          << ", tz=" << scalar_host.tz() << "\n"
          << "vector host: vector=" << vector_host.is_vector()
          << ", values=[" << vector_host.vector()[0]
          << ',' << vector_host.vector()[1] << ']'
          << ", tz=" << vector_host.tz() << "\n";

Output¶

scalar host: scalar=true, value=1709209800000000000, tz=UTC
vector host: vector=true, values=[1709209800000000000,1709251200000000000], tz=UTC

Example 2. A higher-rank payload carries shape and flat row-major data.

auto matrix = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z", "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-03-02T06:15:00Z", ""},
});
const auto host = matrix.host();
const auto& array = host.array();

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "array=" << host.is_array()
          << ", sizes=[" << array.sizes[0] << ',' << array.sizes[1] << ']'
          << ", values=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < array.data.size(); ++i) {
    if (i != 0) std::cout << ',';
    std::cout << array.data[i];
}
std::cout << "]"
          << ", contiguous=" << array.contiguous
          << ", tz=" << array.tz << "\n";

Output¶

array=true, sizes=[2,2], values=[1709209800000000000,1709251200000000000,1709360100000000000,-9223372036854775808], contiguous=true, tz=UTC

The fourth position was constructed from an empty timestamp string and is therefore exported as the exact NaT sentinel.

Example 3. Distinguish source shape from returned payload kind.

auto singleton = pluss::timeline::make({"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z"});
auto host = singleton.host();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "dim=" << singleton.dim()
          << ", is_scalar=" << singleton.is_scalar()
          << ", host scalar=" << host.is_scalar() << "\n";

Output¶

dim=1, is_scalar=false, host scalar=true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Calling scalar(), vector(), or array() on the wrong variant throws.

  • host() allocates and materializes an owning copy. Do not use it merely to inspect rank, count, or timezone metadata.

  • Array data is flat row-major logical order; use array.sizes to recover coordinates.

  • A one-element vector loses its rank in this convenience representation. Use epoch_nanos() when preserving shape is required.
